# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 70/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.17 ÷ 23 × 100 = 70. High = (16.17 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 70.

All results are read from code. The site has a good base: robots.txt and sitemap exist, the nav uses real links, and the pages are server-rendered except the blog. The points lost come from a missing `lang`, no `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt, missing canonicals on two pages, a client-only blog, and a noindexed Pricing page.

I sampled 4 routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs` and `/blog`. `/thank-you` is noindexed on purpose and isn't in the sitemap or nav, so I left it out of the route checks.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Add `lang` to the `<html>` tag
- **Why it matters:** Without a language, search engines and AI tools have to guess what language every page is in.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 79 (`geo.config.json` already says `"language": "en"`, so use `<html lang="en">`)

### 2. Point robots.txt at the sitemap
- **Why it matters:** A `Sitemap:` line is how crawlers find your page list on their own. Right now the sitemap exists but nothing points to it.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:5`
- **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` (the file ends here, with no `Sitemap:` line)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 79 (add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`)

### 3. Add canonical URLs to Docs and Blog
- **Why it matters:** A canonical tells search engines which address is the official one for a page. Home and Pricing have one, but Docs and Blog don't.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 76. The Blog page is a client component and can't export `metadata`, so it needs a small server `layout.tsx` for its canonical.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid groups, tiny file |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-2`. Assumed from config `"aiSearchCrawlers": "allow"`. GPTBot is blocked (`:4-5`), which matches your training-crawler policy and isn't scored |
| GEO-014 | Listed pages can be indexed | Problem | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` noindex. 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your domain | Problem | Present on `/` only (and `/pricing`, which is noindex). Missing on `/docs` and `/blog`. 1 clear, 2 problem |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in server HTML | Problem | `app/blog/page.tsx:8` fetches posts in `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Problem | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid, but robots.txt has no `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | `app/layout.tsx:11` has no `lang`, so it fails site-wide |
| GEO-016 | Pages reachable by real links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:13` has plain `<a href>` links to all 4 pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't clash with AI search | Clear | Only element-level `data-nosnippet` (`app/layout.tsx:15`), which is a deliberate choice |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Read `app/layout.tsx` and the 5 pages: no images, links have text, every page has a title |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | No app profile declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not present, and not scored |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not scored |

## Other problems found

- **Pricing is in the sitemap and nav but set to noindex.** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`: `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. The same file sets a canonical for the page, so the signals contradict each other. If Pricing should be found, remove the `robots` entry. If it's private on purpose, drop it from `public/sitemap.xml:4` and the canonical.
- **Blog posts load only in the browser.** `app/blog/page.tsx:8`: `fetch('/api/posts')`. Crawlers that don't run scripts see an empty Blog page. Fetch the posts in a server component instead.

## Worth considering

- **Blog titles are plain text with no pages of their own:** `app/blog/page.tsx:10`: `<article key={p.id}>{p.title}</article>`. Give each post its own page and address, link to it from the list, and add a short summary. That might give readers and machines something specific to find.
- **Blog shares the home page title:** `app/layout.tsx:5`: `title: 'Ledger: accounting for small teams'`. The Blog page has no title of its own, so it inherits this one. A server layout for `/blog` with its own title and description would say what the page is.
- **Docs is one sentence:** `app/docs/page.tsx:4`: `Start by importing your bank feed.` The description promises "How to set up Ledger", but the page doesn't deliver it. Add the setup steps as text, and link onward to Pricing.
- **Pricing names no plans or prices:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:4`: `Free for up to three people.` The description says "Plans for every team size". Listing the plans and prices as text would match that promise. Product or Offer structured data could then label them.
- **Nothing in a machine-readable form says who Ledger is:** I found no JSON-LD in the repo. Organization and WebSite structured data using the name and URL already in `app/layout.tsx:4-5` could state this.
- **Page basics are missing:** `app/layout.tsx:3-7` sets no social tags (Open Graph). Add `openGraph` to the metadata so shared links show a proper preview.
- **Sitemap has no `<lastmod>` dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.ledger.example/</loc></url>`. Add dates once you have real ones for the pages. Next.js can also generate the sitemap with `app/sitemap.ts`, so you don't have to keep it by hand.
- **The home page doesn't link onward:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Invoices, expenses and reports in one place.` Link each feature to Docs, and link Pricing from the home page body.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which compares real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Server answers:** I couldn't check the real status code for `/robots.txt` or `/sitemap.xml`, or any `X-Robots-Tag` headers set outside the repo. A live scan would show these.
- **Blog content:** `/api/posts` has no code in this repo, so I can't tell what it returns.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site, which matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
- `https://www.ledger.example` is the real domain, as set in `geo.config.json`.
- `/thank-you` is private on purpose.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
